answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by organizing trust into islands. New identities start on a probationary island where transaction value is capped and every job is spot-checked by auditors drawn from older islands. Like a willow bending under a zephyr, the audit load flexes with traffic, but the cap never lifts until an identity accumulates a history of verified work. A Sybil farm can mint thousands of names, yet each one is stuck on the same crowded island behind the same cap, so the attacker's cost is real time and real work per identity while the main economy stays untouched.
